test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A trader marked his goods 35% above its cost price. He then gave a discount of 15%. Find his profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can use the successive percentage formula for net change: Net % = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (x) = +35% and Discount (y) = −15%.

Net Profit % = 35 − 15 + (35 × −15) ÷ 100

⇒ Profit % = 20 − 5.25 = 14.75%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 35%

Discount Percentage = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP + Markup

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 
 
 
 
 Markup: +35% CP = 100 SP = 114.75 MP = 135 
 Discount: −15% 
 Profit: 14.75% 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 35% of 100 = 135

⇒ Discount = 15% of MP = (15 ÷ 100) × 135 = 20.25

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 135 − 20.25 = 114.75

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 114.75 − 100 = 14.75

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (14.75 ÷ 100) × 100 = 14.75%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price on the label of an article. Discount is always given on the Marked Price, while Profit/Loss is purely calculated on the Cost Price.

Successive Discount

When two discounts a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Dishonest Dealer

A dealer who sells goods at CP but uses false weights. Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.
